title: CausalPOI: Spatio-Temporal Graph-Based Causal Modeling for Cold-Start POI Check-in Forecasting

problem.claim: Predict the future check-in pattern of a newly introduced point of interest by modeling its temporal evolution and functional interactions with nearby points of interest in an urban spatial context.

gap.claim: Existing approaches mainly rely on proximity-based graphs and correlation-driven modeling, overlooking functional dependencies between points of interest and causal effects of urban interventions.

contributions.claim: Defines cold-start point-of-interest check-in forecasting as a research problem.
Proposes CausalPOI, a spatio-temporal graph-based causal representation learning framework.

Uses a Spatio-Temporal Functional Interaction Graph and structurally aligned treatment and control graphs to represent semantic and spatial relationships and simulate factual and counterfactual scenarios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly characterize cold-start point-of-interest check-in forecasting as a novel research problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world SafeGraph datasets are reported to show that CausalPOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report effectiveness in spatio-temporal forecasting, semantic interaction modeling, and causal effect estimation.
Source code is reported as available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic point-of-interest modeling is presented as important for urban planning and commercial decision-making.
Prior spatio-temporal graph methods are described as missing functional dependencies and causal intervention effects.
The paper introduces cold-start point-of-interest check-in forecasting.
CausalPOI applies causal representation learning with functional-interaction, treatment, and control graphs.
Experiments and reported code availability are used to support the method's claimed effectiveness and accessibility.

source_observation.claim: The framework models semantic and spatial relationships using functional interaction graphs and uses treatment-control graph structures for factual and counterfactual scenarios.

interpretation.claim: Combining relational structure with explicit counterfactual representations may help address cold-start forecasting when proximity and correlation alone are insufficient.

application.claim: For a new point of interest, represent nearby entities through functional interactions and distinguish observed from counterfactual structural conditions when forecasting.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported SafeGraph datasets or urban intervention settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the forecasting horizon, evaluation metrics, dataset scale, or baseline identities.
The abstract does not describe the causal assumptions, identification strategy, or implementation details.
The abstract does not provide quantitative result values or ablation findings.
